chapter: Arrangers, Bill Robinson and Coleman Hawkins
title: Conducting two Cotton Club shows
summary: Thomas says he conducted two shows after writers made it look like a Broadway production, and rehearsed his short announcing speech.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you want to hold up for a second?
We haven't delved very much into the personnel of the band.
Yeah, right. I'd like to talk about that.
We just got into basically the Cotton Club personnel, the first band. That was three trumpets and three trombones and four saxophones.
Yeah, we finally got the fourth trumpet... I think it was ....(?)....
How many shows did you conduct at the Cotton Club? What did you say?

I think I conducted two. But I didn't conduct the first one downtown. But after the first one... Rube Bloom, I think he had something to do with it -- he was one of the writers. They had the idea of making the show look like a Broadway show. And they decided to write me out of the show, which I was written into the other show...write me out of the show...

Yeah. And then let me be a conductor, go buy me a tuxedo, and let me go and change my tuxedo and be the conductor. Because I had to come out and make some announcements, since(?) Stark was to come on. I used to have to rehearse that speech. It was short. Because all I had to do was just introduce him.
